01

Setting specification

Task

Find an approximate global minimizer, with accuracy measured by suboptimality of the complete objective.

$$\min_{x\in \mathbb{R}^d}f(x)$$

Admissible model

The unknown function $f:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R$ is globally $\beta$-smooth and satisfies $\|\nabla f(x)\|^2\ge2\mu(f(x)-f^\star)$, with $f(x_0)-f^\star\le\Delta$. Nonconvexity is allowed; $\mu$ is the PL constant.

Unless another geometry is specified, vectors use the Euclidean norm $\|\cdot\|_2$, and matrices and higher derivatives use the corresponding operator norm. The assumptions hold uniformly throughout the declared domain.

Here $\beta$-smoothness means $\|\nabla f(u)-\nabla f(v)\|_2\le\beta\|u-v\|_2$ for all $u,v$ in the declared model domain.

Admissible parameter domain: $$\begin{gathered}\varepsilon > 0,\quad d \ge 1,\quad \mu > 0,\quad \kappa \ge 6\\\varepsilon \le c\,\Delta,\quad \beta > 0,\quad \Delta > 0,\quad \sigma \ge 0\\\alpha > 1,\quad \alpha \le 2,\quad \mu \le \beta\end{gathered}$$

Oracle interface

Public numerical inputs: $d,\ \alpha,\ \varepsilon,\ x_0$.

Public upper bounds: $\beta,\ \Delta,\ \sigma$.

Public lower bounds: $\mu$.

The unknown object is the objective $f$.

Query points lie in $\mathbb{R}^d$; feedback consists of stochastic full gradients:

$$\mathbb{E}_tG_t=\nabla f(x_t),\quad\mathbb{E}_t\|G_t-\nabla f(x_t)\|^\alpha\le\sigma^\alpha$$

Samples in a same-point batch are conditionally independent and satisfy the same history-conditional moment bound. No additional independence across adaptively chosen locations is imposed.

Output

Return a point $\widehat x\in\mathbb R^d$.

The output may be unqueried or constructed from the query history, provided it is feasible. No additional function value or accuracy certificate is required.

Loss or accuracy criterion

$$\ell(I,\widehat{x})=f(\widehat{x})-f^\star$$

$f^\star=\inf_{x\in \mathbb{R}^d}f(x)$. The existence, compactness, or initial-suboptimality assumptions ensure that the optimal value in this comparison is finite.

Resource accounting

One full stochastic-gradient sample costs one call; a batch of $b$ samples costs $b$ calls.

Cost is bounded uniformly on every execution path. All calls used for initialization, repetition, batching, or candidate verification are counted.

Real arithmetic, precision, and storage applied to already available information are uncharged. Public geometric operations are limited to those explicitly granted by the oracle. Query complexity alone does not imply arithmetic, memory, or communication complexity.

Algorithm views and success guarantees

Deterministic / Expected loss

The algorithm uses no private random numbers. Query and stopping decisions may depend adaptively on the observed feedback.

No additional span, zero-respecting, linear-iteration, or memory restriction is imposed.

Interaction is adaptive to the feedback history. Every actual response is charged separately, including responses in parallel or batch queries. Internal real arithmetic, storage, and postprocessing are uncharged.

Select an algorithm using the public parameters, and then require the following for every admissible instance and response rule:

$$\forall I\,\forall\mathcal{O}\in\mathcal{O}(I):\ \mathbb{E}_{A,\mathcal{O}}\ell(I,\widehat{x})\le\varepsilon$$

The probability space includes observation noise. The algorithm uses no private random numbers. The instance and its admissible oracle law are fixed before randomness is averaged.

Randomized / Expected loss

Private randomization is allowed. Queries, stopping decisions, and postprocessing may adapt to observed feedback.

No additional span, zero-respecting, linear-iteration, or memory restriction is imposed.

Interaction is adaptive to the feedback history. Every actual response is charged separately, including responses in parallel or batch queries. Internal real arithmetic, storage, and postprocessing are uncharged.

Select an algorithm using the public parameters, and then require the following for every admissible instance and response rule:

$$\forall I\,\forall\mathcal{O}\in\mathcal{O}(I):\ \mathbb{E}_{A,\mathcal{O}}\ell(I,\widehat{x})\le\varepsilon$$

The probability space includes observation noise and the algorithm's private randomness. The instance and its admissible oracle law are fixed before randomness is averaged.

Deterministic / Probability guarantee

The algorithm uses no private random numbers. Query and stopping decisions may depend adaptively on the observed feedback.

No additional span, zero-respecting, linear-iteration, or memory restriction is imposed.

Interaction is adaptive to the feedback history. Every actual response is charged separately, including responses in parallel or batch queries. Internal real arithmetic, storage, and postprocessing are uncharged.

Select an algorithm using the public parameters, and then require the following for every admissible instance and response rule:

$$\forall I\,\forall\mathcal{O}:\ \mathbb{P}(\ell(I,\widehat{x})>\varepsilon)\le\delta$$

The probability space includes observation noise. The algorithm uses no private random numbers. The instance and its admissible oracle law are fixed before randomness is averaged.

Oracle qualification. This view additionally takes the public confidence parameter $\delta$, with $0<\delta<1/2$.

Randomized / Probability guarantee

Private randomization is allowed. Queries, stopping decisions, and postprocessing may adapt to observed feedback.

No additional span, zero-respecting, linear-iteration, or memory restriction is imposed.

Interaction is adaptive to the feedback history. Every actual response is charged separately, including responses in parallel or batch queries. Internal real arithmetic, storage, and postprocessing are uncharged.

The probability space includes observation noise and the algorithm's private randomness. The instance and its admissible oracle law are fixed before randomness is averaged.

02

Notation and parameters

$x,\widehat{x}$

Query points and final output; their permitted spaces are specified separately by the oracle and output contracts

Domain
$\widehat{x}\in \mathbb{R}^d$
$f$

Unknown objective, with domain and structure specified by the model

$\nabla f$

Full gradient of the differentiable objective or smooth term with respect to the decision variable

$x_0$

Public initial point satisfying the stated initial-distance or initial-suboptimality condition

$f^\star$

Optimal value of the complete task; the oracle need not return it

$$f^\star=\inf_{x\in \mathbb{R}^d}f(x)$$

$\mathbb{R}^d$

Real vector space with $d$ coordinates

$\|\cdot\|_2,\langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle$

Euclidean norm and inner product

$G_t$

$t$th full stochastic gradient or subgradient observation

$\mathbb{E}_t$

Conditional expectation given the previous history and current query; the query is selected before the fresh observation is drawn

$d$

Ambient dimension; a positive integer tracked explicitly.

Domain
$d\in\mathbb{N}_{\ge1}$
$\beta$

Public upper bound on the gradient smoothness constant. Any mean-square interpretation is specified in the model.

Domain
$\beta>0$
$\mu$

Known lower bound on the global PL modulus

Domain
$\mu>0$
$\Delta$

Public upper bound on initial suboptimality.

Domain
$\Delta>0$
$\sigma$

Public upper bound on the scale of the conditional centered noise moment.

Domain
$\sigma\ge0$
$\alpha$

Order of the centered noise moment. Every bound with a subscripted constant treats this order as fixed; uniformity as it approaches one is not asserted.

Domain
$1<\alpha\le2$
$\varepsilon$

Target tolerance for the underlying error defined by the accuracy measure

Domain
$\varepsilon>0$
$c$

Sufficiently small universal positive constant, potentially different between theorems; it is not a numerical threshold.

Domain
$0<c<1$
$C$

Sufficiently large universal constant, independent of the tracked parameters; no numerical value is specified.

Domain
$C>1$
$\kappa$

$\beta/\mu$, where $\mu$ is the PL constant; strong convexity is not assumed.

$$\kappa=\frac{\beta}{\mu}$$

$S$

Number of halving stages, $\lceil\log_2(\Delta/\epsilon)\rceil$; not an independent parameter.

$$S=\lceil\log_2(\Delta/\varepsilon)\rceil$$

$V$

Statistical term at the final accuracy scale.

$$V={\frac{{\sigma}^{2}}{\mu\,\varepsilon}}^{\frac{\alpha}{2\,((\alpha-1))}}$$

$d_{\rm hd}$

Sufficient construction dimension in OW26, equation (166): $\widetilde O_\alpha(\kappa^2[\Delta/\epsilon+V])$. Only logarithmic factors are hidden. This is not a necessary dimension threshold.

Domain
$d_{\rm hd}=\widetilde{O}_\alpha(\kappa^2[\Delta/\varepsilon+V])$
$c_\alpha$

Positive multiplicative constant depending only on the fixed $\alpha$; uniform boundedness as $\alpha\downarrow1$ is not asserted.

Domain
$0<c_\alpha<\infty$
$C_\alpha$

Positive multiplicative constant depending only on the fixed $\alpha$; uniform boundedness as $\alpha\downarrow1$ is not asserted.

Domain
$0<C_\alpha<\infty$
$\ell$

The underlying loss or error defined by the accuracy measure; its expected, probabilistic, or worst-case aggregation is specified by the success contract

$I,\mathcal{O},A$

Admissible instance, a response rule consistent with that instance, and an algorithm; the algorithm is selected before the unknown instance

$\mathbb{E}$

Expectation over the declared randomness after fixing the instance and admissible response law

$O,\Omega,\Theta,\widetilde{O},\widetilde\Omega$

Notation for asymptotic upper and lower bounds, constant-factor matching rates, and explicitly permitted logarithmic factors. Hidden-constant dependence is specified in each regime.

$\delta$

Allowed failure probability; expected-error and probability contracts are kept distinct.

Domain
$0<\delta<1/2$
$\Pr,\mathbb{P}$

Event probability after the instance and admissible response law are fixed

$\log$

Natural logarithm; changing to another fixed base affects only a constant

$\Delta_s$

Stage gap target

Domain
$s=0,\ldots,S-1$

$\Delta_s=2^{-s}\Delta$

$q_s$

Stage noise-to-gap ratio

Domain
$q_s\ge0$

$q_s=\sigma^2/(\mu\Delta_s)$

$\mathcal P(\varepsilon)$

Stagewise complexity profile

Domain
$\mathcal P(\varepsilon)>0$

$\mathcal P(\varepsilon)=\sum_{s=0}^{S-1}\min\{\kappa(1+q_s),\kappa^{3/2}+\sqrt\kappa\,q_s\}$

Stagewise switching between robust gradient descent and a gradient-flow trapping routine

Four-Dimensional Stochastic PL Optimization: Stagewise Bounds and Limits of Recursive Constructions ↗
Conditions
$d=4$, $\alpha=2$, $\kappa\ge6$, $\delta=1/4$, $0<\varepsilon\le c_0\Delta$ with the small constant in Corollary optimization-comparison, and $\sigma\ge0$.; Use robust descent when q_s<=sqrt(kappa) and trapping otherwise. Both stage contracts preserve the same gap invariant.
Dimension conditions
Both bounds hold in fixed dimension four.
Algorithm scope
Adaptive randomized algorithms with deterministic sample caps.
Correspondence, constants and qualifications
Constants
Numerical constants only.
Logarithmic factors
The upper logarithmic overhead is displayed; no matching lower logarithm is asserted.
Gap or comparison
The recorded ratio is at most $O([1+\log(4(2+\kappa)(S+1))]^4\mathcal P(\varepsilon)/(S+V))$. For sigma=0 the bounds are Omega(S) versus tilde O(kappa S); in a statistically dominated regime V>=kappa S they are Omega(V) versus tilde O(sqrt(kappa)V).
